title: New Research Finds That Revenue-Maximizing Top Tax Rate Likely Lower Than Previous Estimates
summary: A new paper shows raising top income tax rates on the current tax base may not yield as much revenue as previously estimated, due to opportunities to shift income to different tax bases within the tax code.

title: Property Tax Relief on the Ballot: Three Approaches, One Clear Winner
summary: This November, states across the country are asking voters to consider changes to their state constitutions to address the burden of rising property taxes.

title: A “Token Tax” Could Kill the Promise of AI
summary: If we want to ensure that AI raises economic growth, we shouldn’t be pursuing tax policies that are stuck in the past and represent some of the worst ideas from the early internet age.

title: How Much Does the US Government Lose to Tax Fraud?
summary: While the government will never close the tax gap or fully eliminate tax fraud, lawmakers and the IRS can institute several reforms to reduce the gap, including simplifying the tax code, increasing third-party information reporting, and coordinating anti-fraud efforts.

title: 2027 Tax Foundation Europe Gala
summary: Join us on Monday 27 September 2027 for Tax Foundation Europe’s second annual Gala. Hear from leading experts, network over dinner, and celebrate the pan-European tax policy community.

title: 2027 Tax Foundation Europe Conference
summary: Join us for Tax Foundation Europe’s 2027 Conference, where we will bring together leaders from the international tax community to discuss major tax topics, hear from top academics on new research, and more.

title: Could an Employer Compensation Tax Save Social Security?
summary: With Social Security insolvency rapidly approaching and policymakers exploring changes to benefits and taxation, Congress could look to base-broadening reforms like the ECT as a guide for how to think about taxing compensation and broadening the tax base.

title: Cigarette Taxes and Cigarette Smuggling by State, 2024
summary: Cigarette smuggling is costly for states. We estimate that the forgone revenue from smuggled cigarettes totaled more than $4.6 billion in 2024. California lost nearly $1.4 billion in cigarette excise tax collections, and New York missed out on more than $1.2 billion.

title: Spain’s Tax Competitiveness Has Declined Since 2018
summary: Under Spain’s current Social Democratic government, the country has fallen from 27th to 35th (out of 38 OECD countries) in the International Tax Competitiveness Index.

title: What Is Taxable Income? How It’s Calculated for Tax Filing
summary: Want to know how much you'll owe during tax filing season? Then you need to know your taxable income.

title: In Wyoming, Are Two Homestead Exemptions Enough?
summary: No one enjoys paying taxes, but the property tax serves an important purpose, and Wyoming has already implemented significant property tax relief. Proposition 1 would undercut local finances to a degree that would likely force reliance on worse taxes (local or state) and prompt spending cuts that reduce homeowners’ property values.

title: Options to Reform the Tax Treatment of Exempt Hospitals
summary: Nearly half of all hospitals are exempt from paying US corporate income taxes. As healthcare spending rises, lawmakers have questioned whether hospitals are providing as much in community benefits as they derive from tax exemptions.

title: Expensing Concentrates the Corporate Tax Burden on Economic Profits
summary: As scrutiny over data center investment and AI rises, some commentators are concerned about how expensing interacts with these ongoing investments. Most of these concerns misunderstand what expensing does.

title: 2026 Economics Nobel Laureate Robert Hall Helped Lay Foundation for Pro-Growth Tax Reform
summary: Hall’s research helped economists understand how taxes distort investment decisions, while his work with Rabushka shows how to minimize those distortions. Although the US remains far from a pure consumption tax, Hall’s work informs efforts to reduce the tax burden on investment, improve neutrality, and promote long-run economic growth.

title: Amendment 3: A Restructuring of Florida’s Local Tax Base
summary: Florida has long maintained one of the nation’s most competitive state tax codes, but a fundamental change proposed by Amendment 3 could undermine that competitiveness.

title: International Tax Competitiveness Index 2026
summary: While there are many factors that affect a country's economic performance, taxes play an important role. A well-structured tax code is easy for taxpayers to comply with and can promote economic development while raising sufficient revenue for a government’s priorities.

title: The California Billionaire Tax’s Ever-Shifting Goalposts
summary: Wealth taxes have been a failure everywhere they’ve been tried, which may be why advocates for the California amendment are saying this is a new frontier. But the countries that have tried this gamble know the frontier well, and they’ve left it in the dust.

title: Washington Voters Will Decide Whether to Keep or Reject an Income Tax on High Earners
summary: Washington’s new income tax on high earners doesn’t take effect until 2028, but it is already generating a lot of activity. A measure on the ballot this November, Initiative 645, would reverse the legislature’s decision, preventing the new tax from taking effect.

title: Spain’s Transformation After a Decade of Fiscal Competition
summary: The 2026 Regional Tax Competitiveness Index for Spain highlights a growing divergence between regions that have embraced tax reform and those whose tax systems have remained largely unchanged.

title: Why the US Needs a Fiscal Commission to Help Solve the Debt Crisis
summary: The federal government’s debt burden and interest on the debt are near record levels and headed higher, raising legitimate concerns about an eventual debt crisis. Given the increasingly dysfunctional budget process, the most viable option on the table to stave off such a crisis is a statutory bipartisan fiscal commission with buy-in from leaders of both parties.
